supporting_observations.claim: On WS-MLOPEZ-01, PowerShell ran as omar.haddad with the command to execute \\FILE-HD-01\IT\Deploy-Patches.ps1, matching the organization's documented workstation-patching practice.
The Omar logon on WS-MLOPEZ-01 originated from WS-OHADDAD-01 shortly before PowerShell started, consistent with the documented remote-administration source.
PowerShell launched wusa to install a Windows 11 update package quietly, and Windows Update traffic occurred during the same activity.
The PowerShell process exited about 50 seconds after it started, consistent with the reported brief appearance.

known_telemetry_limitations: The logs establish process creation and termination, but do not show whether or how a PowerShell window was visible to Maria.
The records do not include the contents or a hash of Deploy-Patches.ps1, or confirmation that the update installation completed successfully.
claims_not_established: The available records do not establish that Maria herself launched or saw the PowerShell window.
The available records do not independently verify the script's contents or the update's final installation status.
unrelated_findings: Separate ticket: WS-MLOPEZ-01 obtained Kerberos tickets for ben.carter and WS-BCARTER-01, followed by a network logon to WS-BCARTER-01 from that workstation; investigate whether this cross-account activity was authorized. (T014-00089, T014-00090, T014-00092)
Separate ticket: a network logon for maria.lopez on DC-HD-01 records WS-BCARTER-01 as the workstation. (T014-00112)

Separate ticket: WS-MLOPEZ-01 made connections associated with Google Drive and Dropbox, neither of which is listed as approved software or a service. These records do not establish file transfer or user attribution. (T014-00219, T014-00286)
